detail.longDescription: It seems like Rakudo, the main implementation of the Raku programming language, has been accepting commits written with use of LLM’s for at least a couple of months now. :gutkato_surprizita: I’m not sure what the process has typically been like, but there doesn’t seem to be any formal policy in place, in spite of mentions of AI being used in development dating a while back. I haven’t been able to easily identify the affected commits, but the frequency, verbosity, and comments on some have led me to believe many commit messages may have been generated by LLM’s as well. :gutkato_malesperetas: Even ignoring the many other issues current LLM’s bring with them, being this chill about accepting code you know you might legally not be okay to use, without some explicit note, seems reckless. At the very least, I would have expected this to very much not be okay until it was formally decided otherwise. Or maybe I’m misunderstanding something, but given that a long-term participant has seemingly recently left over too lax of an attitude toward LLM’s, I’m afraid not. :gutkato_malgaja: Raku has long been my favourite programming language by far—progressive and human-friendly in many ways. But if this is the direction it has taken, using it will no longer bring me joy or make me feel cozy and comfortable. So for my personal scripting, I’ll be moving on to other languages. :gutkato_neŭtrala: Which ones? Well, maybe it’s time to dust off my Perl, Raku’s older and not-quite-as-but-still-quite charming sister. Perl doesn’t outright reject LLM contributions, but they’ve adopted a pragmatic yet fairly strict policy around it, which I’m okay with! They’ve been pretty quick about it, too. I might also look into Scheme or something. But I miss my curly quotes very much already, and I’ll have to get used to typing straight ones instead. :gutkato_larmas: #lang_en #AI #LLM #programming #Perl #Perl6 #Raku #Rakudo
